rulings.because: Kamen: approved in bulk 2026-09-05 — reasoning drafted by Claude, adopted by the owner: **1 · buyer-read** and **3 · journalist** (clear vs revise on lines 5–6) — **clear, both.** The two bold lines are a status: "The platform is approved: The Stop Line, decided by Kamen Kamenov." and "The owners and the calendar below are not yet approved; no owner is recorded." The page opens the matching door further down ("Approve the owners and the calendar — Kamen Kamenov before Month 1"), so a buyer or a journalist reads a declared state with a named decider and a deadline, not a contradiction. The version 5 rulings cleared the same lines for the same lenses. **2 · cfo** (clear vs revise on lines 6–8) — **revise.** Line 8 reads "The campaign period is the 12-month approved roadmap year ending no later than 30 June 2027" two lines after "The owners and the calendar below are not yet approved". A funder reads the year called "approved" and the calendar called "not yet approved" in the same breath. The date and the markets are right (the one-pager's "No delivery date is established beyond 30 June 2027"); the word "approved" is the defect, in the writer's period sentence. Revise: the period sentence describes the year without calling it approved while the approval door is open.

Kamen: approved in bulk 2026-09-05 — reasoning drafted by Claude, adopted by the owner: **15 · buyer-read** (clear vs revise on line 7) — **revise.** Three seats already agree the line is a defect (journalist, employee-insider, competitor-counter-position, all on line 7): "signature do words: AI, craftsmanship, enterprise-grade, architect-led, hand-crafted, agentic AI, workflow automations, fit". On a page whose every card says "every AI claim earns its place through approved proof" and whose sign-off row lists "do-not-say lines and final public-claim approval", a list of words the client is told to use — "enterprise-grade", "agentic AI", "workflow automations" — reads to a buyer as the unproven vocabulary the platform exists to hold back. The note is UP's record of the client's own website voice (the six sources listed), appended by the export, not written by the roadmap; that is the boundary to fix. Revise: the style note either states that its do-words are the client's vocabulary and remain subject to the claim boundary, or it does not print on a client-facing deliverable. This is harness work (the export's style-note block), one atom.
